hints.content:
This is the formula for the arc length of a parametric curve over the interval $[a, b]$:

$\displaystyle\int_a^b\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{dx}{dt}\right)^2+\left(\dfrac{dy}{dt}\right)^2}\, dt$

[[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation:
As we zoom in closer to any section of a curve, it begins to resemble a straight line. This means we can use the distance formula to approximate the length of small sections of the curve.

$\blueD{\Delta s} \approx \sqrt{(\purpleD{\Delta x})^2 + (\greenD{\Delta y})^2}$

![The image of a parametric curve with a small section of the curve zoomed in. The zoomed in section resembles a line. The zoomed in section is labeled delta s. A dashed vertical line segment, labeled delta y, extends downward from the right most point of the zoomed in section. A dashed horizontal line segment, labeled delta x, extends from the left most point of the zoomed in section and connects to the dashed vertical line segment.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/cef58cbfc6e0aa6e6b28cbb27604d28061e69824)

Then we can sum all of the segment lengths to approximate the total length.

As we zoom in to infinitely tinier sections, our estimate becomes more accurate. Since our input variable is $t$, we can represent that sum with an integral with respect to $t$:

$\displaystyle\int_a^b\sqrt{\left(\purpleD{\dfrac{dx}{dt}}\right)^2+\left(\greenD{\dfrac{dy}{dt}}\right)^2}\, dt$
options.showPrompt: Where does this formula come from?

hints.content:
Now we can find the expression for the arc length:

$\begin{align}
&\phantom{=}\displaystyle\int_{-5}^{0} \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{dx}{dt}\right)^2+\left(\dfrac{dy}{dt}\right)^2}\,dt
\\\\
&=\displaystyle\int_{-5}^{0} \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{10}{t^3}\right)^2+\left(-e^{-t}\right)^2}\,dt
\\\\
&=\displaystyle\int_{-5}^{0} \sqrt{\dfrac{100}{t^6}+e^{-2t}}\,dt
\end{align}$

In conclusion, this integral gives the arc length of the curve over the interval from $t=-5$ to $t=0$:

$\displaystyle\int_{-5}^{0} \sqrt{\dfrac{100}{t^6}+e^{-2t}}\,dt$

choices.clue: This is $\displaystyle\int_a^b\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{dx}{dt}\right)^2-\left(\dfrac{dy}{dt}\right)^2}\, dt$ but the arc length formula is $\displaystyle\int_a^b\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{dx}{dt}\right)^2+\left(\dfrac{dy}{dt}\right)^2}\, dt$.
